_comment: Up NEPA! dialogue for the Prologue and Act 1. ALL Pidgin, Yoruba, Igbo and Hausa lines are PENDING NATIVE-SPEAKER REVIEW (Story Bible §10). Every person, brand and agency is fictional. Choice: {text, flag?, value?, fx?, reply?: [lines]}.

p1_intro.text: Ojota! Owambe guests! Lekki! Enter with your change!
Driver, I hope this bus has AC. This lace cost me ₦85,000.
Madam, the AC is the window. Wind is free. Baba God dey!
Adeleke, that your aso-ebi is not original. The colour is shouting "Balogun Market".
At least I didn't sew mine last night with candle light.
Ladies, ladies. We will settle it at the jollof.
Everybody hold body. Royal Pavilion, Lekki. We go reach before the couple enter. I promise you.

p1_chinchin.text: Driver, stop small. I want to buy chin-chin for the road.
Mama, the road is the bridge. It is six minutes.
Six minutes is long. My sugar is low.
Which kind sugar? You've been eating my puff-puff since Ojota.
Nobody is stopping. We are on a mission. The mission is jollof.

reply.text: This driver has no home training.
Ah. God bless you, my son. You will marry a good woman.
I'm already married to this bus.

p1_warden.text: Officer Gbenga. My brother. My guy. My personal nightmare.
Your side mirror is facing the wrong spiritual direction. That one is an offence.

p1_warden_pass.text: VIP? Owambe VIP? …Is it the Adeleke wedding? My cousin's wife's sister is catering!
Go, go! Tell them Gbenga said they should keep me moin-moin.
Sule, if you talk two more words this year, I will promote you.

p1_arrive.text: We have arrived in style! In a danfo, but in style!
Driver, come inside. I know the family. Come and chop.
I'm working. I must find passengers for the return…
Nonsense. Free jollof is not something you reject. Sule, you too, come.
…Baba God dey. Sule, lock the bus.

p2_intro.text: Girls! Listen. Elders first. Then the bride's family. Then everybody else.
Anybody who comes with their own takeaway pack, you call me. I will handle them personally.
And nobody, I repeat NOBODY, comes back for a second plate before the couple's family eats. This jollof is politics.

p2_cousin.text: Aunty, I'm the groom's cousin. From abroad. Just flew in. Please add extra chicken, the flight was long.
From… from London. Near London. Around London side.
Ikorodu. I'm from Ikorodu. I came by BRT. Please, one plate, I'm begging.
Join the queue like a citizen. And greet your mother for me.

choices.text: Give him a small plate anyway

reply.text: Aunty, God will bless you. I will tell everybody in London.

p2_debtor.text: Aunty Boss! The food is excellent, as usual. God bless your hands.
Mr. Okafor. You owe me ₦8,000. Since the last owambe. February.
Ah, Aunty, I sent it! Transfer. It must be the network.
It must be. Write it down. I don't forget.

choices.text: "Pay me before the cake is cut."

reply.text: Before the cake. Yes ma. Definitely. Is the cake… far?

p3_intro.text: Wassup wassup, it's your boy KC Vibes, live from the owambe of the YEAR!
Today we are catching three viral moments. Three! The MC, the money spraying and the gele competition.

p3_mc.text: Ladies and gentlemen! Put your hands together for the groom's mother, who will now dance for the THIRD time!
Content! Pure content! The MC is a national treasure.
Where are my money sprayers? Make it rain! Make it pour! Make it flood!

p3_trip.text: And the gele competition is… oh no. Oh NO. The bride's mother!
She tripped on her own gele. On camera. In 4K.
I'm deleting it. I am deleting it right now. Respect for elders.

reply.text: KC deletes it. (He did not delete it.)

p4_mc.text: And now, the moment! The couple's first dance! DJ, give me something for the soul!
Light for All! Terms and conditions apply! Ha ha!
Chief, please, keep your voice down. The bag… the bag is under the table.
Ledger, relax. Who will steal from me in my own mother's friend's daughter's wedding?

p4_light.text: Everybody freeze! Nobody move! …Why is everybody frozen in a dancing pose?
MY BAG! Where is my bag?! LEDGER!
It was here! It was just here! It must be… the opposition! Yes. The opposition did it.
Bro. I recorded EVERYTHING. In the dark. With flash.
Sule. We are going home. Now.
Somebody owes me for forty plates of jollof that disappeared in the dark. I'm writing it down.

m11_intro.text: Sule, today we make money. No owambe, no wahala, no Chief, no bag stories.
Oshodi to Obalende, then back over the bridge. Full bus both ways. Baba God dey!

m11_fares.text: Driver, I gave you ₦1,000 since Oshodi. Where's my change?
Dey come from where? From heaven?
Madam, in this life, change is a journey. Not a destination.

m11_goslow.text: Driver, this go-slow is spiritual. I can see my house from here, and my house is in Ikeja.
Everybody calm down. I know these roads like I know my own pocket. Empty, but I know them.
Wait. I can see it. The gap. The holy gap.

m11_nextime.text: Driver, I no get change. I'll pay you next time.
Next time? Oga, there is no next time in danfo! This is not a subscription!
Next time. God's time is the best.
Sule, two words in one day? What's happening to you?

m11_bag.text: Sule. Sule, come and see. Close the door.
That is the Chief's bag. From the owambe. The one everybody is looking for.
Nobody saw anything. Nobody knows anything. We are not in this.

m12_intro.text: Aunty Boss! Ajo day! The women are ready. Some of them are ready to argue.
Mama Nkem, ajo is trust. Trust is money. And money, I don't forget.
Six women. Six contributions. Nobody leaves the market until I say so.

m12_w1.text: Aunty, here is my ₦5,000. Complete. Count it twice.
I counted it three times while you were bringing it out. Thank you, my sister.

m12_w2.text: Aunty, I'll pay double next week. My tomato spoiled.
Your tomato spoiled last week too. Tomato does not spoil every week.

reply.text: …Here. ₦5,000. Please stop looking at me like that.
Half today, half in my prayers. Thank you, Aunty.

m12_w3.text: Aunty, have you heard? They say the Chief's bag grew legs and walked away.
Gossip is free. Ajo is ₦5,000. Bring it.

m12_w4.text: Aunty, I've transferred it! Look, here's the screenshot.
This screenshot is from 2023. The date is right there. And it's in the old naira design.

choices.text: "You owe me ₦5,000. And now ₦500 for insulting my eyes."

m12_w5.text: My own is ready. And I brought you agbalumo.
This is why you will collect first next month.

m12_w6.text: Last one. Mine. Plus the market council dues.
Mama Nkem, you're the only person in Lagos who has never owed me.
Because I have seen what you do to debtors, my sister.

m12_pos.text: Aunty, the POS queue is long today. And Konnekt network is… you know.
"Network don fail, come back tomorrow." I know. Let me handle it.
When the network fails, tap SWITCH NETWORK or HOLD IT AT THE WINDOW before the customer's patience runs out.

m12_dispute.text: Aunty! This woman says I owe her ₦200 for pepper!
It was ₦200 for pepper AND she touched my tomatoes with her eyes!
Both of you. Silence. The ₦200 dispute will be settled. Today.

choices.text: Split it: ₦100 each, and everybody shakes hands

reply.text: Wisdom. Pure wisdom. Solomon is shaking.

choices.text: Pay the ₦200 yourself to end the noise

reply.text: Aunty Boss is paying? Write it in the newspaper!

choices.text: The Stare. On both of them.

reply.text: …We are no longer quarrelling. We are friends. Since childhood.

m12_whisper.text: Aunty… come closer. Two men came here this morning. One in a red shirt, one big like a fridge.
They were asking for "a canteen woman in the video". The video from the owambe. The one where the light went.
The one with forty thousand views, Aunty. You're in it. Covering a pot.
Write it down. KC Vibes. I don't forget.

m13_intro.text: Guys. GUYS. The blackout clip. Forty thousand viewers. FORTY THOUSAND.
who took the bag 👀  ·  zoom on the table!!  ·  is that a canteen aunty lol
I'm going live right now to break it down frame by frame. Phone battery is at…
…4%. And NEPA has taken light. Again.
Okay. Okay okay okay. Content creators don't panic. We adapt. Somebody in Yaba has power.

m13_barber.text: My generator, my rules. ₦200 to charge. And you must give me your opinion on this haircut.
That is… a bold fade. Very bold. Brave, even.
Thank you! Nobody appreciates art in this area. Plug in.

m13_church.text: You can charge. The church has an inverter. But you must sit until the end of the prayer.
Pastor started at 9. It's 11. We are on point 3 of 12.
😂😂 bro is trapped  ·  AMEN  ·  type 1 for blessings

m13_kiosk.text: Charge Am Here! Thirty phones, one socket, zero wahala.
It's not smoking. It's thinking. ₦100, plug in.

m13_reveal.text: Okay chat, frame 412. Look at the hand going under the table. That's the bag. And that face is…
That face is the CHIEF'S OWN TREASURER. The man is—
??? continue!!!  ·  KC??  ·  it froze  ·  he don japa 😭
Guys… guys? The signal. The signal dropped exactly there. Of course it did.

m13_pepper.text: Hey! You! Purple shirt! You're the boy in the video!
Me? No. I'm his twin. He's in Abuja. Like and subscribe!
Come here! The Chief wants to "discuss content" with you!

m13_canteen.text: Aunty, please, there's a man chasing me, I just need five minutes—
You are KC Vibes. You filmed me covering my pot in the dark. Forty thousand people have seen my elbow.
You owe me an explanation. And ₦2,500 for the malt you're about to drink. Sit. Food is ready.

m14_intro.text: Two men came to the park. Red shirt. Big man. They asked for a yellow danfo.
Sule, every danfo in Lagos is yellow.
With "Baba God Dey" on the back.
…Okay. We need to hide the bus. Alhaji Mechanic in Mushin. He owes me.

m14_passenger.text: Driver, I am going to Mushin. I have paid. Full journey.
Madam, today is not a good day. Please come down.
I have paid for the full journey. I am not coming down. I will be filing my nails.
Pepper and Salt are coming. Keep them away. Passengers will shout directions: vote on the turns. The heat meter shows how close they are.

m14_hide.text: Alhaji! Cover the bus! Now now now!
Tunde, you still owe me for the last gearbox.
Your account is a book. A full book.
This is my stop. Thank you, driver. Five stars. Very exciting service.
We need help. Somebody with sense.
I know one woman in Surulere. Her canteen has a generator and she fears nobody.

m15_open.text: So. A danfo driver, a content creator, and a bag of money. In my canteen. At night.
Madam, I just need somewhere to keep it for one night. One night!
Aunty, the whole internet is looking for this bag. I can make it a series—
Nobody is filming anything inside my canteen. Generator! Somebody add fuel!

m15_standoff.text: The bag was under seat 4! I didn't steal anything!
I have the video! It was the treasurer! Ledger!
Lower your voices, my customers are sleeping upstairs!
If the Chief finds this bag with us, we're finished!
If the internet finds it with us, we're FAMOUS!
If either of you breaks my plate, you're both finished AND famous!
We should hide it somewhere nobody will look!
We should give it back with a camera running!
We should count it! Nobody makes decisions about money they haven't counted!

m15_bag.text: Wait. Bring that bag here. Look at this handle.
This stitching. Double cross, then a knot. This is MY stitching. I sewed this bag. Three years ago. For a client.
A man who paid with "transfer, I've sent it". I never forgot his face.
Tunde, you've gone quiet. Tunde doesn't go quiet.
I'm just tired. Long day. What do we do with it?

m15_return.text: The next morning, at the Chief's campaign office…
You want to return a bag? To the Chief? Which bag?
The Chief has not lost any bag. The Chief has never had a bag. Who sent you?
Go away before we arrest you for… for… bringing a bag.
So they can't admit it's theirs. Interesting. Write it down.

m15_count.text: Nobody decides anything about money that hasn't been counted. Tunde, the rubber bands. KC, put down that phone and count.

m15_diary.text: Wait. What's this? Stuck between the notes… a page.
"Paid: Rally ₦4.5m. Paid: 'consultants' ₦12m. Paid: Light for All transformer… ₦0."
It's a diary. Somebody wrote down everything.
Somebody who doesn't forget. I like this person already.

m15_hide.text: Under the rice. Nobody looks under fifty kilos of rice.
Thieves who want my rice will meet my Stare.

m15_close.text: Listen, both of you. From today, we talk every day. Nobody does anything alone.
No group chat. Group chats are where peace goes to die.
